definitions.explanation: A way of cutting vegetables and other ingredients into stick or baton shapes, typically about 4-5 cm long and 1 cm square in cross-section. Named after its resemblance to hyoushigi (wooden clappers used in traditional Japanese performances).

examples.japanese: ⟦{大根|だいこん}→大根：05186_daikon⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{拍子木|ひょうしぎ}{切|ぎ}り⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Cut the daikon radish into baton shapes.

examples.japanese: にんじん⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{拍子木|ひょうしぎ}{切|ぎ}りにして、⟦サラダ→サラダ：01364_sarada⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{入|い}れた→入れる：01098_ireru⟧。
examples.english: I cut the carrot into sticks and put them in the salad.

examples.japanese: ⟦{煮物|にもの}→煮物：04971_nimono⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{材料|ざいりょう}→材料：02831_zairyou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、{拍子木|ひょうしぎ}{切|ぎ}り⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{火|ひ}→火：02248_hi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{通|とお}り→通り：01475_toori⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{均一|きんいつ}→均一：12049_kinitsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: If you cut the simmered dish ingredients into baton shapes, they cook evenly.

notes:
A standard Japanese cooking cut named after {拍子木|ひょうしぎ}, the wooden clappers used in kabuki and by night watchmen. The resulting pieces are rectangular sticks, typically 4-5 cm long and about 1 cm square. Knowing cutting terminology is essential for following Japanese recipes.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{大根|だいこん}→大根：05186_daikon⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{拍子木|ひょうしぎ}{切|ぎ}り: baton-cut daikon
- にんじん⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{拍子木|ひょうしぎ}{切|ぎ}り⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to cut carrots into batons
- {拍子木|ひょうしぎ}{切|ぎ}りにした⟦{野菜|やさい}→野菜：02265_yasai⟧: vegetables cut into sticks

RELATED CUTTING TERMS:
- ⟦{千切|せんぎ}り→千切り：07473_sengiri⟧: julienne cut (thin strips)
- ⟦{乱切|らんぎ}り→乱切り：08067_rangiri⟧: irregular cut (random chunks)
- ⟦{短冊|たんざく}{切|ぎ}り→短冊切り：08087_tanzakugiri⟧: rectangular strip cut
- {賽|さい}の{目|め}{切|ぎ}り: dice cut (small cubes)
- ⟦{輪切|わぎ}り→輪切り：07474_wagiri⟧: round slices
